A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RefAV and RefProg. Their text, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original baseline evaluations, LLM ablations, sampling-rate experiments and dataset analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds baseline evaluations, nuPrompt results, token-cost measurements and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The central program-synthesis-and-track-filtering procedure remains. v3 adds SigLIP2 visual-attribute access and an is_color function absent from v1's API. Its nuPrompt adaptation changes the category list and excludes map-dependent functions while retaining the remaining atomic definitions.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates tracking methods on RefAV; v3 additionally evaluates RefProg on nuPrompt, introducing nuScenes data and its referential expressions. Appendix C also analyzes sampled expressions from nuPrompt, Refer-KITTI and nuScenes-QA. The underlying RefAV coverage remains 1,000 driving logs and 10,000 log-prompt pairs.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes RefInflate/GroundingDINO and adds caption-based ReferGPT, GPT-5 black-box inference and three challenge submissions. Table 4 adds nuPrompt comparisons with CenterPoint Tracker, DQTrack, ADA-Track and PromptTrack. RefBlind and RefClassify are retained as Filter by Referred Class and Image-Embedding Similarity, respectively.

E3.justification: New protocols include nuPrompt evaluation with StreamPETR and AMOTA, AMOTP, recall and MOTA; GPT-5-based cost comparisons; and embedding-based farthest-point sampling of 30 expressions per dataset. Existing RefAV HOTA/balanced-accuracy metrics and 2 Hz evaluation are retained. These additions do not establish reruns of the retained experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds token/cost analysis in Appendix B, systematic qualitative dataset comparison in C, per-scenario occurrence analysis in G, and three successful plus three unsuccessful synthesized-program case studies in I. The earlier LLM, related/other-object and sampling-rate analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. Added dataset frequencies and token measurements do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Shared RefProg/Le3DE2E performance remains 50.1 HOTA-Temporal. v3 adds ReferGPT at 20.2, GPT-5 black-box inference at 37.2 and the leading challenge entry at 53.4 in Table 2, and RefProg/StreamPETR at 0.321 AMOTA on nuPrompt in Table 4. RefInflate's 4.0 result disappears. New cost results use different LLM configurations. Table 1 also changes RefAV frames from 15,500 to 155k and nuPrompt expressions from 40,776 to 407k; these are not equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix A adds explicit mathematical definitions for ReferGPT's motion-feature vector and weighted matching score, s = s_cosine + 0.1 s_fuzzy. This is a limited formal specification addition; neither version develops theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central RefAV benchmark and program-synthesis contributions remain. The abstract and introduction replace the prospective challenge contribution with analysis of completed community results. The nuPrompt discussion additionally claims cross-dataset generalization and state-of-the-art zero-shot accuracy.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations involving vehicle-class dominance, CLIP sensitivity to predicted boxes, ReferGPT's missing temporal context, and token efficiency from code scaffolding. Its case studies distinguish expressivity, semantic and logical failures. It also argues for cross-dataset applicability while removing v1's explicit runtime/scalability limitation and shortening the dataset-annotation limitations.

D1.justification: v3 supplies detailed ReferGPT and GPT-5 prompts, model identifiers, reasoning/tool settings, cropping and scoring rules, and synthesized-program examples. It newly documents annotation effort and generation success rate. Challenge-report access is added, while v1's direct tracker-output download link is removed; the main code and dataset links remain.

R1.justification: The main related-work discussion is largely retained. v3 adds citations for ADA-Track, DQTrack, SigLIP2, StreamPETR and CenterPoint, and removes GroundingDINO. Appendix C elaborates RefAV's planning-oriented positioning through sampled comparisons with existing driving-language datasets.

P1.justification: Baseline and empirical-analysis explanations are substantially rewritten, including replacement of RefBlind/RefClassify terminology. Section 4 consolidates formerly separate metrics, ablation, challenge and limitations subsections. The supplement is reorganized from Appendices A–F into A–J, although much of the introduction, related work and conclusion remains.

P2.justification: v3 adopts two-column layout throughout, redraws the problem-setup and dataset-creation figures, relocates and reformats retained illustrations and tables, and adds nuPrompt and cost tables plus a scenario-occurrence chart. Existing distribution plots and supplementary performance tables are mostly reformatted or moved rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The nuPrompt evaluation tests portability beyond RefAV's shared generation/mining API, while actual ReferGPT and GPT-5 comparisons strengthen baseline validation. Detailed implementation, cost and failure analyses substantially improve assessability and reproducibility. Drawbacks include removal of the runtime caveat, different decoders in the nuPrompt comparison, and unexplained ReferGPT scores of 20.2 versus 20.7 across Tables 2 and 5. These limit particular conclusions but do not outweigh the substantial validation and documentation gains.
